medicines.excretion: Mainly renal excretion of unchanged drug.

medicines.pediatric: Weight-based dosing in children.

medicines.memory_trick: "-tidine" → H2 blocker.

medicines.description: A proton pump inhibitor with rapid onset used in acid-related disorders.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+-ATPase proton pump in parietal cells.

medicines.distribution: Highly protein bound.
medicines.metabolism: Hepatic metabolism, largely non-enzymatic with some CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 involvement.

May mask gastric cancer symptoms
monitoring: Symptom control and need for continued therapy
medicines.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children under specialist advice.
medicines.geriatric: Review the need for long-term therapy.
medicines.hepatic: Reduce dose in severe hepatic impairment.
key_points: Take 30-60 minutes before the first meal of the day
medicines.memory_trick: "-prazole" → proton pump inhibitor; take before food.

medicines.description: A prokinetic antiemetic that does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Blocks dopamine D2 receptors in the gut and in the chemoreceptor trigger zone, which lies outside the blood-brain barrier.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Increases gastric emptying and lower oesophageal tone with a low risk of extrapyramidal effects.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed but with extensive first-pass metabolism.
medicines.distribution: Poor penetration into the central nervous system.
medicines.excretion: Faecal and renal excretion of metabolites.
warnings: Use the lowest effective dose for up to one week where possible
QT prolongation and sudden cardiac death risk at higher doses
drug_interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole and clarithromycin
monitoring: ECG when risk factors are present
medicines.pregnancy: Avoid unless clearly necessary.
medicines.lactation: Small amounts pass into milk; medical advice needed.
medicines.pediatric: Restricted in children; specialist decision.
medicines.geriatric: Higher cardiac risk; keep doses low and courses short.
medicines.hepatic: Avoid in moderate to severe hepatic impairment.
disadvantages: QT prolongation limits dose and duration
key_points: Prefer short courses at the lowest effective dose
medicines.memory_trick: Domperidone stays outside the brain — gut relief without dystonia.

medicines.description: A dopamine antagonist antiemetic and prokinetic.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Blocks central and peripheral dopamine D2 receptors and, at higher doses, 5-HT3 receptors; also has 5-HT4 agonist prokinetic activity.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Antiemetic and prokinetic; crosses the blood-brain barrier so extrapyramidal effects can occur.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed orally.
medicines.distribution: Widely distributed including the CNS.
indications: Aid to intubation of the small bowel
warnings: Restrict to a maximum of 5 days where possible
Acute dystonic reactions are more common in young women and children
Tardive dyskinesia with prolonged use
medicines.pregnancy: Used when benefit outweighs risk; commonly used for hyperemesis under supervision.
medicines.lactation: Small amounts in milk; short-term use usually acceptable.
medicines.pediatric: Restricted; higher risk of dystonia in children.
key_points: Treat acute dystonia promptly with an anticholinergic such as promethazine or benztropine
medicines.memory_trick: Metoclopramide crosses into the brain — dystonia is the price.

medicines.description: An antimotility agent for symptomatic control of non-infective diarrhoea.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Agonist at peripheral mu-opioid receptors in the intestinal wall, slowing transit and increasing water absorption.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Antidiarrhoeal without central opioid effects at normal doses because of P-glycoprotein efflux at the blood-brain barrier.
medicines.absorption: Poorly absorbed systemically.
medicines.distribution: Acts locally in the gut; minimal CNS penetration at therapeutic doses.
medicines.metabolism: Extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4 and CYP2C8.

contraindications: Suspected dysentery or C. difficile colitis
warnings: Do not use in dysentery
High doses cause serious cardiac arrhythmias
Oral rehydration remains the priority in acute diarrhoea
serious_adverse_effects: QT prolongation and cardiac arrest in overdose
medicines.pregnancy: Avoid in the first trimester unless essential.
medicines.lactation: Small amounts in milk; short-term use usually acceptable.
medicines.pediatric: Not for children under 4 years.
key_points: Fluid and electrolyte replacement matters more than stopping the stools
medicines.memory_trick: Loperamide = "lock the pipe" — never in bloody diarrhoea.

medicines.description: An osmotic laxative also used in hepatic encephalopathy.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: A non-absorbed disaccharide fermented by colonic bacteria into organic acids that draw water into the bowel and acidify colonic contents.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Softens stool and increases frequency; traps ammonia as ammonium in hepatic encephalopathy.
medicines.absorption: Not absorbed from the gut.
medicines.distribution: Remains within the intestinal lumen.
medicines.metabolism: Metabolised by colonic bacteria to lactic and acetic acid.
warnings: Flatulence and cramps are common in the first days
Titrate to 2-3 soft stools daily in hepatic encephalopathy
medicines.pregnancy: Considered safe in pregnancy.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children with weight-based dosing.
key_points: In hepatic encephalopathy the dose is titrated to stool frequency, not to a fixed number
medicines.memory_trick: Lactulose = "sugar the gut bacteria eat" — acid traps ammonia.

medicines.description: A mucosal protectant that coats ulcer bases.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: In acidic conditions it polymerises and binds to proteins at the ulcer base, forming a protective barrier; also stimulates prostaglandin and mucus production.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Local cytoprotection without significant acid suppression.
medicines.absorption: Minimal systemic absorption.
medicines.distribution: Acts locally on the gastric and duodenal mucosa.
medicines.excretion: Excreted mainly in faeces; small amounts of aluminium absorbed.
warnings: Take on an empty stomach, 1 hour before meals
Separate from other medicines by at least 2 hours
medicines.pregnancy: Considered low risk; minimal absorption.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children under medical advice.
advantages: Acts locally with minimal systemic effect
key_points: Space all other oral medicines away from sucralfate
medicines.memory_trick: Sucralfate = a bandage for the ulcer, needs acid to stick.

medicines.description: The active enantiomer of cetirizine, a second-generation antihistamine.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Selective peripheral histamine H1 receptor inverse agonist.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Relieves allergic symptoms with less sedation than first-generation agents, though some drowsiness occurs.
medicines.absorption: Rapid and near-complete oral absorption.
medicines.distribution: Limited CNS penetration; small volume of distribution.
medicines.excretion: Mainly renal excretion of unchanged drug.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to cetirizine or hydroxyzine
warnings: Can still cause drowsiness — caution when driving
Avoid alcohol
medicines.pregnancy: Use only when clearly needed.
medicines.lactation: Small amounts in milk; medical advice needed.
medicines.pediatric: Approved for children with age-based dosing.
medicines.geriatric: Reduce dose if renal function is reduced.
medicines.renal: Reduce dose or interval in renal impairment.
medicines.hepatic: No routine adjustment unless renal function is also impaired.
disadvantages: More sedating than fexofenadine or loratadine
key_points: Chronic urticaria may need higher specialist-directed doses
medicines.memory_trick: Levocetirizine = the "left-handed" half of cetirizine.

medicines.description: A non-sedating second-generation antihistamine.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Selective peripheral H1 receptor antagonist that does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Relieves allergic symptoms with essentially no sedation at usual doses.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed; fruit juices markedly reduce absorption.
medicines.distribution: Poor CNS penetration; P-glycoprotein substrate.
medicines.excretion: Mainly faecal excretion with some renal excretion.
warnings: Avoid taking with grapefruit, orange or apple juice
Separate from aluminium and magnesium antacids by 2 hours
medicines.pregnancy: Use only when clearly needed.
medicines.pediatric: Approved for children with age-based dosing.
medicines.geriatric: Well tolerated; adjust for renal function.
advantages: Least sedating of the common antihistamines
disadvantages: Absorption reduced by fruit juice and antacids
key_points: Take with water, not with fruit juice
medicines.memory_trick: Fexofenadine = "fewer effects on the brain".

medicines.description: A first-generation sedating antihistamine widely used in cold and allergy preparations.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Competitive H1 receptor antagonist with additional antimuscarinic activity; crosses the blood-brain barrier.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Relieves allergic symptoms and causes sedation and drying of secretions.
medicines.absorption: Well absorbed orally.
medicines.distribution: Crosses the blood-brain barrier and the placenta.
warnings: Marked sedation — avoid driving or operating machinery
Anticholinergic effects are troublesome in the elderly
serious_adverse_effects: Confusion and falls in the elderly
medicines.pregnancy: Used when needed; discuss with a clinician.
medicines.lactation: Can cause infant drowsiness; seek medical advice.
medicines.pediatric: Avoid in infants; caution in young children.
medicines.geriatric: Avoid where possible — falls and confusion risk.
key_points: Adrenaline, not an antihistamine, is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis
medicines.memory_trick: First-generation antihistamines = "sleepy and dry".

medicines.description: An oral leukotriene receptor antagonist used as add-on asthma therapy.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks the cysteinyl leukotriene CysLT1 receptor, reducing bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion and eosinophilic inflammation.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Modest bronchodilation and anti-inflammatory effect; useful in exercise-induced and allergic asthma.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed orally.
medicines.distribution: Highly protein bound.
medicines.metabolism: Extensive hepatic metabolism via CYP2C8, CYP3A4 and CYP2C9.
warnings: Neuropsychiatric events including mood change, nightmares and suicidal thinking have been reported
Not for acute asthma attacks
medicines.pregnancy: Considered acceptable when needed for asthma control.
medicines.pediatric: Approved from 6 months with age-based dosing.
medicines.hepatic: Caution in moderate to severe hepatic impairment.
advantages: Useful when inhaler technique is poor
key_points: Take in the evening; stop and seek advice if mood or sleep changes
medicines.memory_trick: "-lukast" → leukotriene blocker.

medicines.description: An inhaled corticosteroid used as controller therapy in asthma.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Binds glucocorticoid receptors in airway cells, suppressing transcription of inflammatory mediators.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Reduces airway inflammation, hyper-responsiveness and exacerbation rate over days to weeks.
medicines.absorption: Deposited in the airway; a swallowed fraction is absorbed from the gut.
medicines.distribution: Distributes to airway tissue; high first-pass metabolism limits systemic exposure.
medicines.metabolism: Extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4.
medicines.excretion: Renal and faecal excretion of metabolites.
medicines.bioavailability: About 10-15% of an inhaled dose reaches the systemic circulation
warnings: Not a reliever — it does not relieve an acute attack
Rinse the mouth after each dose to prevent oral thrush
serious_adverse_effects: Reduced growth velocity in children with high doses
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole and ritonavir
medicines.pregnancy: Inhaled corticosteroids are generally continued in pregnancy.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children with age-appropriate devices and spacers.
medicines.geriatric: Effective; watch for local side effects.
medicines.hepatic: Systemic exposure rises in severe hepatic impairment.
key_points: Use a spacer and rinse the mouth to reduce candidiasis
medicines.memory_trick: Inhaled steroid = "prevent, not rescue" — rinse after use.

medicines.description: A short-acting inhaled anticholinergic bronchodilator.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Blocks muscarinic M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle, reducing vagally mediated bronchoconstriction and mucus secretion.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Bronchodilation with slower onset but longer duration than salbutamol; minimal systemic absorption.
medicines.absorption: Poorly absorbed from the airway and gut.
medicines.distribution: Acts locally in the airways; quaternary structure limits systemic distribution.
medicines.metabolism: Partial hepatic metabolism of absorbed drug.
warnings: Avoid contact with the eyes — nebulised drug can precipitate acute glaucoma
Caution in bladder outflow obstruction
serious_adverse_effects: Acute angle-closure glaucoma with eye exposure
medicines.pregnancy: Considered acceptable when needed.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children with weight and age-based dosing.
medicines.geriatric: Useful in COPD; watch anticholinergic effects.
advantages: Adds benefit to salbutamol in acute severe asthma and COPD
key_points: Use a well-fitting mask or mouthpiece to keep the drug out of the eyes
medicines.memory_trick: Ipratropium = "atropine for the airways".

medicines.description: A central cough suppressant used for dry, non-productive cough.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Acts on the medullary cough centre, raising the threshold for the cough reflex; it is a sigma-1 agonist and NMDA antagonist without opioid analgesic activity.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Suppresses dry cough within about 30 minutes; no analgesic or significant dependence liability at therapeutic doses.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed orally.
medicines.distribution: Widely distributed including the CNS.
medicines.metabolism: Hepatic metabolism via CYP2D6 to dextrorphan; poor metabolisers have higher levels.
contraindications: Concurrent or recent MAO inhibitor use
warnings: Abuse potential at high doses
Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs
Do not use for cough with copious sputum
drug_interactions: CYP2D6 inhibitors such as fluoxetine and quinidine
medicines.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed.
medicines.lactation: Short-term use usually considered acceptable; seek advice.
medicines.pediatric: Not for children under 4 years.
key_points: Never suppress a wet, productive cough
medicines.memory_trick: Dextromethorphan = "DM" on cough syrup labels — dry cough only.

medicines.description: A second-generation sulfonylurea used in type 2 diabetes.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Binds the SUR1 subunit of pancreatic beta-cell KATP channels, causing depolarisation, calcium influx and insulin release.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Lowers blood glucose by stimulating endogenous insulin secretion; effect depends on residual beta-cell function.
medicines.absorption: Well absorbed orally; the modified-release form gives a smoother profile.
medicines.distribution: Highly protein bound.
medicines.metabolism: Extensive hepatic metabolism to inactive metabolites.

Weight gain is common

medicines.pediatric: Not used in children.
medicines.geriatric: Prefer the lowest dose; high hypoglycaemia risk.
disadvantages: Loses effect as beta-cell function declines
key_points: Advise patients on sick-day and fasting rules
medicines.memory_trick: "-ide" sulfonylureas → squeeze insulin out of the pancreas.

medicines.description: A DPP-4 inhibitor that raises incretin levels in type 2 diabetes.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits dipeptidyl peptidase-4, preventing breakdown of GLP-1 and GIP, which increases glucose-dependent insulin release and lowers glucagon.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Modest HbA1c reduction with a low intrinsic risk of hypoglycaemia and a neutral effect on weight.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed; food has no clinically important effect.
medicines.distribution: Moderate volume of distribution.
medicines.excretion: Mainly renal excretion of unchanged drug.

Severe joint pain has been reported
Dose reduction needed in renal impairment

medicines.pediatric: Not established in children.
medicines.geriatric: Well tolerated; adjust for renal function.
medicines.renal: Reduce dose in moderate to severe renal impairment.
medicines.hepatic: No routine adjustment in mild to moderate impairment.
advantages: Low hypoglycaemia risk when used alone
key_points: Stop and investigate if severe persistent abdominal pain occurs
medicines.memory_trick: "-gliptin" → DPP-4 inhibitor, incretin helper.

medicines.description: An SGLT2 inhibitor with benefits in diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 in the proximal renal tubule, reducing glucose reabsorption and increasing urinary glucose excretion.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Lowers glucose independently of insulin; produces mild diuresis, weight loss and blood pressure reduction with cardiorenal benefit.

medicines.excretion: Renal and faecal excretion of metabolites.

Euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis can occur; withhold during acute illness, fasting or surgery
Volume depletion risk with diuretics
medicines.pregnancy: Not recommended in pregnancy.
medicines.pediatric: Not established in children.
medicines.geriatric: Watch for volume depletion and hypotension.
medicines.renal: Glucose-lowering effect falls with low eGFR, but cardiorenal benefit persists.
disadvantages: Ketoacidosis risk during illness or fasting

medicines.description: A thiazolidinedione that improves insulin sensitivity.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Activates PPAR-gamma nuclear receptors, altering transcription of genes involved in glucose and lipid metabolism and improving peripheral insulin sensitivity.

medicines.distribution: Highly protein bound.
medicines.metabolism: Hepatic metabolism via CYP2C8 and CYP3A4 to active metabolites.

contraindications: Active bladder cancer or unexplained haematuria
warnings: Fluid retention can precipitate heart failure
Increased fracture risk, particularly in women
Weight gain is common

medicines.pediatric: Not established in children.

medicines.renal: No dose adjustment, but avoid if on dialysis.
disadvantages: Oedema, weight gain and heart failure risk

medicines.memory_trick: "-glitazone" → PPAR-gamma; think oedema and weight gain.

medicines.description: Short-acting soluble insulin used in daily regimens and emergencies.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Binds insulin receptors, promoting cellular glucose uptake, glycogen and protein synthesis, and suppressing hepatic glucose production and lipolysis.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Onset about 30 minutes subcutaneously with a peak at 2-3 hours; immediate action when given intravenously.

medicines.distribution: Distributed in extracellular fluid.
medicines.metabolism: Degraded by insulinase in liver, kidney and muscle.
medicines.half_life: About 1.5 hours in plasma; longer clinical action

warnings: Inject 30 minutes before meals
Rotate injection sites to prevent lipohypertrophy
Never share pens or needles
medicines.pregnancy: Insulin is the preferred glucose-lowering therapy in pregnancy.
medicines.lactation: Compatible with breastfeeding; doses often need reduction.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children with careful dose titration.

medicines.renal: Insulin requirement falls in renal impairment.
medicines.hepatic: Requirement may change in hepatic impairment.
advantages: Effective in every form of diabetes
key_points: Unopened vials go in the fridge; the in-use vial can stay at room temperature for about 28 days
medicines.memory_trick: Regular insulin = the only insulin routinely given intravenously.

medicines.description: An antithyroid drug used to control hyperthyroidism.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Converted to methimazole, which inhibits thyroid peroxidase and blocks iodination and coupling of thyroglobulin tyrosine residues.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Reduces new thyroid hormone synthesis; clinical effect takes 2-6 weeks because stored hormone must be depleted.

medicines.distribution: Concentrated in the thyroid gland.

contraindications: Previous agranulocytosis or severe reaction to thionamides

Congenital malformations reported with first-trimester use
monitoring: Full blood count if infection symptoms occur

medicines.pediatric: Used in children under specialist care.

medicines.memory_trick: Carbimazole → "Cuts hormone production; Check the throat".

medicines.description: A widely used oral corticosteroid with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Binds cytoplasmic glucocorticoid receptors, altering transcription of genes controlling inflammation and immune activation.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Broad anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive activity with predominantly glucocorticoid and mild mineralocorticoid effect.

Raises blood glucose and blood pressure
Increases infection risk and can mask its signs

medicines.description: A potent long-acting corticosteroid with negligible mineralocorticoid activity.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Binds glucocorticoid receptors, suppressing transcription of pro-inflammatory genes; about 25-30 times more potent than hydrocortisone.

medicines.pediatric: Used in croup as a single oral dose.
medicines.geriatric: Monitor glucose and infection risk closely.

medicines.memory_trick: Dexamethasone = strongest and longest of the common steroids, no salt retention.

medicines.description: An ACE inhibitor prodrug used in hypertension and heart failure.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Its active metabolite enalaprilat inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, reducing angiotensin II formation and aldosterone release and decreasing bradykinin breakdown.

medicines.metabolism: Hepatic hydrolysis of the prodrug to enalaprilat.

Angioedema can be life threatening
Check renal function and potassium after starting or increasing the dose
monitoring: Serum creatinine and potassium 1-2 weeks after initiation

medicines.lactation: Alternatives are preferred; seek specialist advice.
medicines.pediatric: Used in children under specialist care.

medicines.description: A long-acting ACE inhibitor with strong cardiovascular outcome evidence.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Hydrolysed to ramiprilat, which inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, lowering angiotensin II and aldosterone.

Symptomatic hypotension after the first dose
Renal function and potassium must be checked after initiation

medicines.pediatric: Specialist use only in children.
medicines.geriatric: Start low; monitor blood pressure standing and sitting.

medicines.memory_trick: "-pril" → ACE inhibitor; ramipril is the outcome-trial workhorse.

medicines.description: An angiotensin receptor blocker used in hypertension and heart failure.

Hyperkalaemia and renal impairment risk as with ACE inhibitors
Do not combine with an ACE inhibitor

medicines.pediatric: Used in children over 6 years under specialist care.

disadvantages: Same pregnancy and potassium cautions as ACE inhibitors
key_points: ARBs are the usual switch when an ACE inhibitor causes cough

medicines.description: A dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used in hypertension and angina.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle, causing arterial vasodilation.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Reduces peripheral resistance and blood pressure; immediate-release forms can cause reflex tachycardia.
medicines.absorption: Rapidly absorbed; extensive first-pass metabolism.
medicines.distribution: Highly protein bound.

contraindications: Within one month of myocardial infarction (immediate release)

Do not take with grapefruit juice
Swallow modified-release tablets whole
medicines.pregnancy: Used in pregnancy for hypertension and tocolysis under supervision.
medicines.pediatric: Specialist use in children.
key_points: Never use sublingual nifedipine for a hypertensive crisis
medicines.memory_trick: "-dipine" → dihydropyridine; ankle swelling and flushing.

medicines.description: A cardioselective beta blocker used in hypertension and angina.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks beta-1 adrenoceptors, reducing heart rate, contractility and renin release.

Can mask hypoglycaemia symptoms in diabetes

Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor

medicines.description: Lincosamide antibiotic active against Gram-positive cocci and anaerobes.

Diarrhoea must always be taken seriously

medicines.description: Oxazolidinone antibiotic active against resistant Gram-positive organisms including MRSA and VRE.

Serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs

Weekly blood counts during therapy

medicines.description: Aminoglycoside antibiotic used for serious Gram-negative infections resistant to gentamicin.

Irreversible ototoxicity and vestibular damage
Neuromuscular blockade

Once-daily dosing reduces toxicity

medicines.description: Glycopeptide antibiotic for serious Gram-positive infections including MRSA.

Oral therapy for Clostridioides difficile colitis

Ototoxicity at high levels

Oral and intravenous forms treat completely different problems

medicines.description: Triazole antifungal used for dermatophyte, nail and systemic fungal infections.

Hepatotoxicity
Potent CYP3A4 inhibition with many interactions

Absorption depends on stomach acid

medicines.description: Imidazole antifungal now used mainly topically because of systemic hepatotoxicity.

Modern practice is topical use

medicines.description: Allylamine antifungal and first-line treatment for dermatophyte nail and skin infection.

Full blood count in long courses

Short courses relative to nail growth

First-line for dermatophyte onychomycosis

medicines.description: Topical imidazole antifungal for skin, vaginal and oral candidal infections.

Weakens latex barrier contraceptives

medicines.description: Imidazole antifungal used topically and as an oral gel for candidiasis.

Even the oral gel interacts with warfarin

medicines.description: Polyene antifungal for severe systemic fungal infections and visceral leishmaniasis.

Electrolytes must be watched daily

medicines.description: Oral prodrug of aciclovir with better bioavailability, used for herpes and varicella zoster infections.

Neurotoxicity in renal impairment

Early start improves zoster outcomes
medicines.memory_trick: Valacyclovir = aciclovir with a "delivery van" attached. Learning aid — exceptions exist.

Reduction in bone mineral density
Severe hepatitis B flare if stopped abruptly

Do not stop abruptly in hepatitis B

Never stop suddenly in hepatitis B

medicines.description: Nucleoside analogue used for chronic hepatitis B with a high barrier to resistance.

medicines.description: Long-acting nitroimidazole given as a single dose for amoebiasis, giardiasis and bacterial vaginosis.

Repeat dose after 2 weeks for threadworm

medicines.description: Thiazolide antiparasitic used for giardiasis, cryptosporidiosis and some infectious diarrhoeas.

medicines.memory_trick: "-sartan" → ARB; blocks the receptor, no cough. Learning aid — exceptions exist.

medicines.description: Cardioselective beta blocker used in hypertension, angina and heart failure.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Selectively blocks beta-1 adrenergic receptors, reducing heart rate, contractility and renin release.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Lowers blood pressure and myocardial oxygen demand; improves survival in chronic heart failure.
medicines.absorption: Well absorbed with little first-pass effect.
medicines.distribution: Volume of distribution about 3.5 L/kg.
medicines.excretion: Renal and hepatic in roughly equal parts.
warnings: Never stop abruptly — rebound angina and arrhythmia
May mask hypoglycaemia symptoms
precautions: Start low and titrate slowly in heart failure
serious_adverse_effects: Worsening heart failure during rapid titration
medicines.pregnancy: Used when necessary with monitoring.
medicines.lactation: Considered compatible with monitoring of the infant.
medicines.pediatric: Limited paediatric data.
key_points: "-olol" marks beta blockers
One of the four heart failure beta blockers
medicines.memory_trick: "-olol" → beta blocker; never stop suddenly. Learning aid — exceptions exist.

medicines.description: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker for angina, hypertension and rate control.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Blocks L-type calcium channels in cardiac and vascular smooth muscle, slowing AV nodal conduction and causing vasodilation.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Reduces heart rate, contractility and blood pressure; relieves coronary vasospasm.
medicines.absorption: Well absorbed with extensive first-pass metabolism.
medicines.distribution: Volume of distribution about 3-13 L/kg.
medicines.metabolism: Hepatic via CYP3A4; also a CYP3A4 inhibitor.
contraindications: Severe bradycardia or second/third degree heart block
Sick sinus syndrome without a pacemaker
warnings: Do not combine with intravenous beta blockers
Bradycardia and heart block risk
CYP3A4 inhibition raises other drug levels
medicines.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed.
medicines.pediatric: Limited paediatric use.
advantages: Useful when beta blockers are contraindicated in asthma
key_points: Non-dihydropyridine calcium blocker
Avoid combining with beta blockers for rate control
medicines.memory_trick: Diltiazem and verapamil = "heart-slowing" calcium blockers. Learning aid — exceptions exist.

medicines.description: Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker with the strongest cardiac depressant effect of the class.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Blocks L-type calcium channels, markedly slowing AV nodal conduction and reducing contractility.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Rate control, antianginal and antihypertensive effects.
medicines.absorption: Well absorbed but extensive first-pass metabolism.
medicines.distribution: Volume of distribution about 3-5 L/kg.
medicines.metabolism: Hepatic via CYP3A4; potent CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibitor.
contraindications: Second or third degree heart block
warnings: Severe bradycardia and asystole risk with intravenous use plus beta blockers
Marked constipation
Raises digoxin levels
precautions: Advise fluid and fibre for constipation
medicines.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed.
medicines.pediatric: Specialist use in children.
medicines.geriatric: Start low; constipation and bradycardia risk.
medicines.renal: Caution; reduce dose in severe impairment.
advantages: Effective rate control and antianginal action
key_points: Most cardiodepressant calcium channel blocker
Constipation is the classic side effect
medicines.memory_trick: Verapamil = "very constipating" calcium blocker. Learning aid — exceptions exist.

medicines.description: Thiazide-like diuretic with a long duration of action used for hypertension.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits sodium-chloride reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, promoting sodium and water loss.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Sustained blood pressure reduction with proven cardiovascular outcome benefit.
medicines.absorption: Well absorbed; slow onset.
medicines.distribution: Concentrates in red blood cells.
warnings: Electrolyte disturbance, especially hyponatraemia and hypokalaemia
Hyperuricaemia may precipitate gout
Raises blood glucose
medicines.pregnancy: Not first choice; use only if necessary.
medicines.pediatric: Rarely used in children.
medicines.geriatric: Higher hyponatraemia risk; use low doses.
advantages: Longer acting and more potent than hydrochlorothiazide
key_points: Thiazide-like diuretic
Low doses give most of the benefit
medicines.memory_trick: Chlorthalidone = "long-acting thiazide-like" — check the sodium. Learning aid — exceptions exist.

medicines.description: Loop diuretic with more predictable absorption and longer action than furosemide.
medicines.mechanism_of_action: Inhibits the Na-K-2Cl co-transporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.
medicines.pharmacodynamics: Potent diuresis with reliable oral bioavailability; also mild antihypertensive effect.
medicines.absorption: Rapid, near complete absorption largely unaffected by food or oedema.
medicines.distribution: Volume of distribution about 12-15 L.
indications: Oedema in renal or hepatic disease
warnings: Electrolyte depletion and dehydration
Ototoxicity with rapid high-dose intravenous use
precautions: Take in the morning to avoid nocturia
medicines.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed.
medicines.pediatric: Limited paediatric data.
medicines.renal: Higher doses often needed; monitor closely.
key_points: Loop diuretic
Bioavailability is more reliable than furosemide in heart failure
medicines.memory_trick: Loop diuretics = "torrential urine, check potassium". Learning aid — exceptions exist.

drug_classes.name: Analgesics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that reduce or relieve pain.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dard ko kam ya relieve karne wali dawa ko analgesic kehte hain.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents that relieve pain without causing loss of consciousness.

drug_classes.name: Antimicrobials
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that kill or stop germs.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Infection paida karne wale germs ko maarne ya rokne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents active against bacteria, fungi, viruses or parasites.

drug_classes.name: Gastrointestinal Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for stomach and gut problems.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Pet, acidity, ulti aur digestion se judi dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents acting on the gastrointestinal tract.

drug_classes.name: Cardiovascular Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for heart and blood pressure.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dil aur blood pressure se judi dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents acting on the heart, vessels and circulation.

drug_classes.name: Respiratory Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for breathing problems.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Saans aur asthma se judi dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents acting on the airways and respiratory system.

drug_classes.name: Endocrine & Metabolic Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for hormones, diabetes and thyroid.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Hormone, diabetes aur thyroid se judi dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents modifying endocrine and metabolic function.

drug_classes.name: Allergy & Immunology
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for allergy and immune reactions.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Allergy aur immune reaction ki dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents modifying allergic and immune responses.

drug_classes.name: Blood & Haematology
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines affecting blood clotting.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Khoon jamne ki process par asar karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents modifying haemostasis and blood constituents.

drug_classes.name: Lipid-Lowering Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that lower cholesterol.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Cholesterol kam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents reducing plasma lipid levels.

drug_classes.name: Non-Opioid Analgesics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Pain relievers that are not opioids.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Wo painkillers jo opioid nahi hote.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Analgesic agents acting without opioid receptor agonism.
drug_classes.mechanism: Central COX inhibition and other central mechanisms (paracetamol).
advantages: Generally well tolerated at therapeutic doses

drug_classes.name: NSAIDs
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Pain and inflammation medicines.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dard aur soojan dono kam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs inhibiting cyclo-oxygenase enzymes.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit COX-1/COX-2, reducing prostaglandin synthesis.
advantages: Anti-inflammatory in addition to analgesic effect
disadvantages: Gastrointestinal and renal adverse effects with prolonged use

drug_classes.name: Beta-Lactam Antibiotics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Antibiotics that break bacterial cell walls.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Bacteria ki deewar todne wale antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antibiotics containing a beta-lactam ring that inhibit cell wall synthesis.
drug_classes.mechanism: Bind penicillin-binding proteins, inhibiting peptidoglycan cross-linking.

drug_classes.name: Macrolides
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Antibiotics that stop bacteria making proteins.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Bacteria ka protein banna rokne wale antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Macrocyclic lactone antibiotics binding the 50S ribosomal subunit.
drug_classes.mechanism: Bind 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibit bacterial protein synthesis.

drug_classes.name: Tetracyclines
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Broad antibiotics that stop bacterial protein production.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics jo bacteria ka protein banna rokte hain.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antibiotics binding the 30S ribosomal subunit.
drug_classes.mechanism: Bind 30S subunit, blocking aminoacyl-tRNA attachment.
disadvantages: Not suitable in pregnancy or young children

drug_classes.name: Nitroimidazoles
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for anaerobic bacteria and some parasites.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Anaerobic bacteria aur kuch parasites ke liye dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents activated in anaerobic organisms causing DNA damage.
drug_classes.mechanism: Reduced nitro group forms reactive intermediates damaging microbial DNA.

drug_classes.name: Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPI)
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Strong acid-reducing medicines.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Pet ka acid strongly kam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Irreversible inhibitors of the gastric H+/K+-ATPase.
drug_classes.mechanism: Irreversibly inhibit the gastric proton pump in parietal cells.

drug_classes.name: Antiemetics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that stop vomiting.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Ulti rokne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents preventing or relieving nausea and vomiting.
drug_classes.mechanism: 5-HT3 receptor antagonism (setrons) and other pathways.

drug_classes.name: Antihistamines (H1)
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Allergy medicines.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Allergy ki dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: H1 receptor inverse agonists/antagonists.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block histamine H1 receptors, reducing allergic response.

drug_classes.name: Beta-2 Agonist Bronchodilators
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that open airways.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Saans ki naliyon ko kholne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Selective beta-2 adrenoceptor agonists relaxing bronchial smooth muscle.
drug_classes.mechanism: Stimulate beta-2 receptors, increasing cAMP and relaxing airway smooth muscle.
disadvantages: Not anti-inflammatory; overuse signals poor control

drug_classes.name: Biguanides
drug_classes.simple_explanation: First-line diabetes tablets.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Diabetes ki first-line tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antihyperglycaemic agents reducing hepatic glucose output.
drug_classes.mechanism: Reduce hepatic gluconeogenesis and improve insulin sensitivity (AMPK-related).

drug_classes.name: Sulfonylureas
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Diabetes tablets that push insulin release.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Insulin release badhane wali diabetes tablets.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents closing pancreatic beta-cell K-ATP channels.
drug_classes.mechanism: Close K-ATP channels, depolarising beta cells and releasing insulin.

drug_classes.name: Calcium Channel Blockers
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Blood pressure medicines that relax vessels.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Blood vessels ko relax karke BP kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents blocking L-type calcium channels.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation.
advantages: Effective in Indian and elderly populations

drug_classes.name: Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers (ARB)
drug_classes.simple_explanation: BP medicines that block a vessel-tightening hormone.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Blood vessel tight karne wale hormone ko block karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antagonists of the angiotensin II type 1 receptor.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block AT1 receptors, preventing angiotensin II mediated vasoconstriction.

drug_classes.name: ACE Inhibitors
drug_classes.simple_explanation: BP medicines that block an enzyme.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Ek enzyme ko block karke BP kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of angiotensin-converting enzyme.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit ACE, reducing angiotensin II and aldosterone.

drug_classes.name: Loop Diuretics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Strong water-removing medicines.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Sharir se extra paani nikalne wali strong dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of the Na-K-2Cl transporter in the loop of Henle.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb, causing marked diuresis.

drug_classes.name: Statins
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Cholesterol-lowering medicines.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Cholesterol kam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, upregulating hepatic LDL receptors.

drug_classes.name: Antiplatelet Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that stop platelets sticking together.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Platelets ko chipakne se rokne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents inhibiting platelet aggregation.
drug_classes.mechanism: COX-1 inhibition (aspirin) or P2Y12 receptor blockade (clopidogrel).

drug_classes.name: Thyroid Hormone Replacement
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Replaces a missing thyroid hormone.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Thyroid hormone ki kami poori karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Synthetic thyroid hormone replacement therapy.
drug_classes.mechanism: Provides exogenous T4 converted peripherally to active T3.

drug_classes.name: Central Nervous System Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that act on the brain and nerves.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dimaag aur nerves par asar karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents acting on the central nervous system.

drug_classes.name: Musculoskeletal & Antigout Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for joints, muscles and gout.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Jodo, muscles aur gout ki dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents used in musculoskeletal and crystal arthropathy disorders.

drug_classes.name: Vitamins & Minerals
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Supplements that correct deficiencies.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Sharir me kami poori karne wale supplements.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Micronutrient and haematinic supplementation agents.

drug_classes.name: Genitourinary Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for urinary and prostate problems.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Peshaab aur prostate se judi dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents acting on the urinary tract and prostate.

drug_classes.name: Opioid Analgesics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Strong pain medicines acting on the brain.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dimaag par asar karke tez dard kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agonists at opioid receptors used for moderate to severe pain.
drug_classes.mechanism: Agonism at mu-opioid receptors reduces pain transmission and perception.
disadvantages: Dependence and respiratory depression risk; controlled drugs

drug_classes.name: Penicillins
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Beta-lactam antibiotics of the penicillin group.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Penicillin group ke beta-lactam antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Beta-lactam antibiotics derived from the penicillin nucleus.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit penicillin-binding proteins and bacterial cell wall cross-linking.

drug_classes.name: Cephalosporins
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Beta-lactam antibiotics of the cephalosporin group.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Cephalosporin group ke beta-lactam antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Beta-lactam antibiotics grouped into generations by spectrum.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit cell wall synthesis via penicillin-binding proteins.

drug_classes.name: Fluoroquinolones
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Antibiotics that block bacterial DNA copying.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Bacteria ka DNA banna rokne wale antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antibacterials inhibiting DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication.
disadvantages: Tendon and neurological safety concerns; resistance

drug_classes.name: Aminoglycosides
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Injectable antibiotics for serious infections.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Serious infection ke liye injectable antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antibiotics binding the 30S ribosomal subunit, causing misreading of mRNA.
drug_classes.mechanism: Bind 30S subunit irreversibly, causing mistranslation and cell death.

drug_classes.name: Sulfonamides & Trimethoprim
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Antibiotics that block bacterial folate production.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Bacteria ka folate banna rokne wale antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antibacterials inhibiting sequential steps of bacterial folate synthesis.
drug_classes.mechanism: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; trimethoprim inhibits dihydrofolate reductase.

drug_classes.name: Nitrofuran Urinary Antiseptics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Antibiotics that mainly work in the bladder.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Mukhya roop se bladder me kaam karne wale antibiotics.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Urinary antibacterials concentrated in urine.
drug_classes.mechanism: Reduced by bacterial nitroreductases to reactive intermediates damaging bacterial macromolecules.
disadvantages: Not suitable for kidney or systemic infection

drug_classes.name: Antitubercular Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that treat tuberculosis.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: TB ka ilaaj karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents active against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, used in combination regimens.
drug_classes.mechanism: Varied: RNA polymerase inhibition (rifampicin), mycolic acid synthesis inhibition (isoniazid).
advantages: Curative when the full regimen is completed

drug_classes.name: Antifungals
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for fungal infections.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Fungal infection ki dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents active against pathogenic fungi.
drug_classes.mechanism: Azoles inhibit fungal CYP51 (14-alpha-demethylase), impairing ergosterol synthesis.
advantages: Oral options available for many infections

drug_classes.name: Antivirals
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that act against viruses.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Virus ke khilaf kaam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents inhibiting viral replication.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit viral enzymes such as DNA polymerase or neuraminidase.
key_adverse_effects: Renal effects at high IV doses
advantages: Reduce severity and duration when started early
disadvantages: Timing dependent; limited benefit if started late

drug_classes.name: Anthelmintics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that remove worms.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Pet ke keede nikalne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents active against helminth parasites.
drug_classes.mechanism: Benzimidazoles inhibit parasite tubulin polymerisation; ivermectin acts on glutamate-gated chloride channels.
disadvantages: Reinfection is common without hygiene measures

drug_classes.name: Antimalarials & Related Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines used in malaria and some autoimmune diseases.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Malaria aur kuch autoimmune bimariyon me use hone wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: 4-aminoquinolines and related agents.
drug_classes.mechanism: Interfere with parasite haem detoxification; immunomodulatory effects in rheumatic disease.
disadvantages: Requires eye monitoring on long-term use

drug_classes.name: H2 Receptor Antagonists
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Acid-reducing medicines weaker than PPIs.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: PPI se halki, acid kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Competitive antagonists at gastric parietal cell H2 receptors.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block histamine H2 receptors, reducing gastric acid secretion.
advantages: Rapid onset; useful for on-demand relief
disadvantages: Less potent than PPIs; tolerance can develop

drug_classes.name: Prokinetics & Dopamine Antagonist Antiemetics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that help the stomach empty and stop vomiting.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Pet khali karne me madad aur ulti rokne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Dopamine D2 antagonists increasing gastric motility.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block dopamine D2 receptors in the gut and chemoreceptor trigger zone.
disadvantages: Neurological and cardiac safety limits on duration

drug_classes.name: Antidiarrhoeals
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that slow down diarrhoea.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dast kam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents reducing intestinal motility or secretion.
drug_classes.mechanism: Peripheral mu-opioid receptor agonism slows intestinal transit.
disadvantages: Must not be used in invasive/infective diarrhoea

drug_classes.name: Laxatives
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that relieve constipation.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Kabz door karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents promoting bowel evacuation.
drug_classes.mechanism: Osmotic, stimulant or bulk-forming actions on the bowel.

drug_classes.name: Mucosal Protectants & Antacids
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that coat or neutralise stomach acid.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Pet ki lining ko cover karne ya acid neutralise karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents forming a protective barrier or neutralising gastric acid.
drug_classes.mechanism: Form a protective coating over ulcer bases or chemically neutralise gastric acid.
disadvantages: Frequent dosing; reduces absorption of other drugs

drug_classes.name: Leukotriene Receptor Antagonists
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Tablets that reduce airway inflammation in asthma.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Asthma me airway ki soojan kam karne wali tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Selective cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 receptor antagonists.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block CysLT1 receptors, reducing bronchoconstriction and inflammation.
disadvantages: Not for acute attacks; neuropsychiatric warnings

drug_classes.name: Inhaled Corticosteroids
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Inhalers that reduce airway inflammation.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Airway ki soojan kam karne wale inhaler.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Topically active corticosteroids delivered to the airways.
drug_classes.mechanism: Bind glucocorticoid receptors, reducing airway inflammatory gene expression.
disadvantages: Requires correct technique and mouth rinsing

drug_classes.name: Anticholinergic Bronchodilators
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Inhalers that open airways by blocking a nerve signal.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Nerve signal block karke airway kholne wale inhaler.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Muscarinic receptor antagonists causing bronchodilation.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block muscarinic M3 receptors on airway smooth muscle.
advantages: Useful add-on in COPD and acute asthma

drug_classes.name: Cough Preparations
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines for cough.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Khansi ki dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antitussive and expectorant agents.
drug_classes.mechanism: Central suppression of the cough reflex (antitussives).

drug_classes.name: DPP-4 Inhibitors
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Diabetes tablets that boost natural insulin signals.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Natural insulin signals badhane wali diabetes tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of dipeptidyl peptidase-4.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit DPP-4, prolonging incretin (GLP-1, GIP) activity.
advantages: Weight neutral; low hypoglycaemia risk alone

drug_classes.name: SGLT2 Inhibitors
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Diabetes tablets that remove sugar in urine.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Peshaab ke through sugar nikalne wali diabetes tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of the sodium-glucose co-transporter 2.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block SGLT2 in the proximal tubule, increasing urinary glucose excretion.
disadvantages: Genital infections; ketoacidosis risk in illness

drug_classes.name: Thiazolidinediones
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Diabetes tablets that improve insulin sensitivity.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Insulin sensitivity badhane wali diabetes tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: PPAR-gamma agonists.
drug_classes.mechanism: Activate PPAR-gamma, improving peripheral insulin sensitivity.
advantages: Durable glycaemic effect; no hypoglycaemia alone
disadvantages: Oedema, weight gain and heart failure risk

drug_classes.name: Insulins
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Injectable hormone that lowers blood sugar.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Blood sugar kam karne wala injectable hormone.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Exogenous insulin preparations.
drug_classes.mechanism: Activate insulin receptors, promoting glucose uptake and suppressing hepatic glucose output.
advantages: Effective in all forms of diabetes

drug_classes.name: Antithyroid Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that reduce thyroid hormone production.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Thyroid hormone banna kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Thionamide inhibitors of thyroid peroxidase.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit thyroid peroxidase, reducing thyroid hormone synthesis.
disadvantages: Requires warning about sore throat and fever

drug_classes.name: Systemic Corticosteroids
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Strong anti-inflammatory hormone medicines.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Soojan bahut kam karne wali hormone dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Synthetic glucocorticoids with anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive activity.
drug_classes.mechanism: Bind glucocorticoid receptors, altering transcription of inflammatory genes.
disadvantages: Wide-ranging adverse effects; needs tapering after prolonged use

drug_classes.name: Beta Blockers
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that slow the heart and lower BP.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Heart rate aur BP kam karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Antagonists at beta-adrenergic receptors.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block beta-1 (and sometimes beta-2) adrenoceptors, reducing heart rate and contractility.
advantages: Outcome benefit in heart failure and post-MI
disadvantages: Avoid abrupt withdrawal; caution in asthma

drug_classes.name: Thiazide & Thiazide-like Diuretics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Mild water tablets used for blood pressure.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: BP ke liye use hone wali halki water tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of the Na-Cl co-transporter in the distal tubule.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block the distal convoluted tubule Na-Cl symporter, increasing sodium and water excretion.

drug_classes.name: Potassium-Sparing Diuretics & Aldosterone Antagonists
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Water tablets that keep potassium in the body.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Potassium bachane wali water tablet.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Aldosterone receptor antagonists and ENaC blockers.
drug_classes.mechanism: Antagonise mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal nephron.

drug_classes.name: Cardiac Glycosides
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Old heart medicines that strengthen and slow the heartbeat.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Dil ki dhadkan slow aur strong karne wali purani dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of the sodium-potassium ATPase with positive inotropic effect.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit Na+/K+-ATPase, raising intracellular calcium; increased vagal tone slows AV conduction.
advantages: Useful for rate control in atrial fibrillation with heart failure
disadvantages: Narrow therapeutic index; toxicity worsened by hypokalaemia

drug_classes.name: Anticoagulants
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that thin the blood.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Khoon patla karne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents inhibiting the coagulation cascade.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit vitamin K-dependent clotting factor synthesis or potentiate antithrombin.
disadvantages: Bleeding risk; warfarin needs INR monitoring

drug_classes.name: Fibrates
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that mainly lower triglycerides.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Mukhya roop se triglycerides kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: PPAR-alpha agonists.
drug_classes.mechanism: Activate PPAR-alpha, increasing lipoprotein lipase activity and fatty acid oxidation.

drug_classes.name: Antiepileptics
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that prevent seizures.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Mirgi ke daure rokne wali dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents reducing neuronal hyperexcitability.
drug_classes.mechanism: Sodium channel blockade, GABA enhancement or synaptic vesicle protein modulation.

drug_classes.name: Benzodiazepines
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Calming medicines that also stop seizures.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Shaant karne wali aur daure rokne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Positive allosteric modulators of the GABA-A receptor.
drug_classes.mechanism: Enhance GABA-A mediated chloride conductance, increasing inhibition.
advantages: Rapid effect in status epilepticus and acute anxiety

drug_classes.name: Tricyclic Antidepressants
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Older antidepressants also used for nerve pain.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Purani antidepressant jo nerve pain me bhi use hoti hai.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Inhibitors of noradrenaline and serotonin reuptake with antimuscarinic activity.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block noradrenaline and serotonin reuptake; also block muscarinic, histaminergic and alpha-1 receptors.
advantages: Useful in neuropathic pain at low doses

drug_classes.name: SSRIs
drug_classes.simple_explanation: First-line antidepressants.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: First-line antidepressant dawaiyan.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.
drug_classes.mechanism: Selectively inhibit presynaptic serotonin reuptake, increasing synaptic serotonin.
advantages: Better tolerated and safer in overdose than TCAs

drug_classes.name: Urate-Lowering Agents
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that lower uric acid in gout.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Gout me uric acid kam karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors and uricosurics.
drug_classes.mechanism: Inhibit xanthine oxidase, reducing uric acid production.
contraindications: Acute gout attack (do not start during a flare without cover)
disadvantages: Flares on initiation; serious rash is a stop signal

drug_classes.name: Haematinics & Supplements
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Iron, folate and vitamin supplements.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Iron, folic acid aur vitamin supplements.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Agents supplying substrates for haematopoiesis and micronutrient needs.
drug_classes.mechanism: Provide iron or folate required for haemoglobin and DNA synthesis.

drug_classes.name: Alpha-1 Blockers
drug_classes.simple_explanation: Medicines that relax the prostate and bladder outlet.
drug_classes.hindi_explanation: Prostate aur bladder outlet relax karne wali dawa.
drug_classes.clinical_definition: Selective alpha-1 adrenoceptor antagonists.
drug_classes.mechanism: Block alpha-1 adrenoceptors in prostatic and bladder neck smooth muscle.
disadvantages: First-dose hypotension; floppy iris during cataract surgery

medical_terms.definition: A medicine used to relieve pain.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dard ko kam ya relieve karne wali dawa ko analgesic kehte hain.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that reduces fever.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Bukhar kam karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug that reduces pain, fever and inflammation.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dard, bukhar aur soojan kam karne wali non-steroid dawa.
medical_terms.hinglish_explanation: Pain + swelling dono kam karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that kills or inhibits bacteria.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Bacteria ko maarne ya rokne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine active against viruses.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Virus ke khilaf kaam karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine active against fungal infections.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Fungal infection ki dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that blocks histamine receptors, used in allergy.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Allergy me use hone wali dawa jo histamine ko block karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: An agent that neutralises gastric acid.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Pet ke acid ko neutralise karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: Proton pump inhibitor; strongly reduces gastric acid secretion.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Pet ka acid banna strongly kam karne wali dawa.
medical_terms.hinglish_explanation: Acid production hi kam kar deti hai.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that increases urine output.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Peshaab zyada karwa kar extra paani nikalne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine blocking beta-adrenergic receptors.
medical_terms.simple_definition: Slows the heart and lowers BP.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Heart rate aur BP kam karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine inhibiting angiotensin-converting enzyme.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: ACE enzyme ko block karke BP kam karti hai.
medical_terms.hinglish_explanation: BP ki medicine, kabhi khansi karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: Angiotensin II receptor blocker.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Angiotensin receptor ko block karke BP kam karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine blocking L-type calcium channels.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Blood vessels relax karke BP kam karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that reduces blood clot formation.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Khoon jamne ki process ko dheema karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine preventing platelet aggregation.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Platelets ko aapas me chipakne se rokti hai.

medical_terms.definition: An HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that lowers LDL cholesterol.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Cholesterol kam karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A steroid hormone analogue with anti-inflammatory action.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Soojan ko strongly kam karne wali steroid dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine widening the airways.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Saans ki naliyon ko chaudi karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that thins mucus.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Gaadhe balgam ko patla karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: An agent aiding the expulsion of airway secretions.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Balgam bahar nikalne me madad karne wali dawa.
medical_terms.hinglish_explanation: Balgam nikalne me help karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine that suppresses cough.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Sookhi khansi ko dabane wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: An agent producing calming effects.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Shant karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: An agent that induces sleep.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Neend laane wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine used in depressive disorders.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Depression ke ilaj me use hone wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine used in psychotic disorders.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Psychosis ke ilaj me use hone wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine used to prevent seizures.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Mirgi ke daure rokne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: A medicine preventing nausea and vomiting.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Ulti rokne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: An agent promoting bowel evacuation.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Kabz door karne wali dawa.

medical_terms.definition: An agent applied to living tissue to reduce infection risk.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Skin par lagane wala germ-killer.

medical_terms.definition: An agent applied to non-living surfaces to destroy microbes.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Surfaces ke liye germ-killer.

medical_terms.definition: A substance that binds a receptor and produces a response.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Receptor se judkar usko activate karne wala.

medical_terms.definition: A substance that binds a receptor and blocks a response.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Receptor ko block karne wala.

medical_terms.definition: A cellular protein to which a drug binds to produce an effect.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Wo protein jahan dawa judti hai.
medical_terms.hinglish_explanation: Drug ka lock, drug is the key.

medical_terms.definition: A substance that reduces the activity of an enzyme.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Enzyme ki activity kam karne wala.

medical_terms.definition: Time required for plasma drug concentration to fall by half.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dawa ka level aadha hone me lagne wala samay.

medical_terms.definition: Fraction of an administered dose reaching systemic circulation unchanged.
medical_terms.simple_definition: How much actually reaches the blood.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dawa ka kitna hissa khoon tak pahunchta hai.

medical_terms.definition: Volume of plasma cleared of drug per unit time.
medical_terms.simple_definition: How fast the body removes a drug.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Body kitni tezi se dawa hataati hai.

medical_terms.definition: Apparent volume into which a drug distributes.
medical_terms.simple_definition: How widely a drug spreads in the body.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dawa body me kitni faili hai.

medical_terms.definition: Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion.
medical_terms.simple_definition: The drug's journey through the body.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dawa ka body me safar: absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion.

medical_terms.definition: What the body does to the drug.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Body dawa ke saath kya karti hai.

medical_terms.definition: What the drug does to the body.
medical_terms.hindi_explanation: Dawa body ke saath kya karti hai.
